docs.title: OMPA
docs.text:
Universal AI Agent Memory Layer — Vault · Palace · Temporal Knowledge Graph

OMPA gives any AI agent persistent memory in one pip install. It combines three layers:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 1: Vault  — human-navigable markdown          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Layer 2: Palace — agent-accessible metadata         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Layer 3: Knowledge Graph — temporal SQLite triples  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Verbatim storage plus local hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings). Measured on the full LongMemEval-S (n=470): R@5 0.979 for hybrid search and 0.970 for keyword-only search. See benchmarks/README.md.

docs.text:
pip install ompa          # Core
pip install ompa[all]     # Core + local semantic search

docs.title: Audit memory
docs.text:
OMPA can keep a tamper-evident, append-only audit log of everything that changes agent memory. It can attach provenance to every retrieval and every fact, answer "what did the agent know at time T", enforce retention, legal hold and right-to-erasure policies, and enforce per-vault access control.

Everything here is stdlib-only (SQLite + hashlib/hmac). Ed25519 signing needs the optional cryptography package: pip install ompa[audit].

Supports, not certifies

OMPA provides technical controls that support compliance programmes (see Compliance mapping). Using OMPA does not make a system compliant or certified with any regulation or standard. Certification and attestation depend on your whole system, your processes and an assessor.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from ompa import Ompa

ao = Ompa(vault_path="./vault", audit=True, principal="agent-7")   # audit on
ao.write("Kai owns the Orion budget. [[Kai]]", file_path="work/orion.md")
ao.kg_add("Kai", "works_on", "Orion")

hit = ao.search("Orion budget")[0]
hit.citation      # path, line/byte span, content_sha256, author, recorded_at, valid_from/to
ao.kg_query("Kai")[0].citation

report = ao.audit_verify()          # {"ok": True, "shared": {...chain report + drift...}}
head = ao.audit_head()              # store this OUTSIDE the vault (anchor)

with ao.as_of("2026-10-21T08:00:00Z") as view:   # transaction time, UTC
    view.facts("Kai")                             # what was known then

ao.forget("Zorblatt Quince")        # right to erasure (admin), tombstone kept

CLI:

ao audit enable --vault-path ./vault          # migrate an existing vault (baseline snapshot)
ao audit keygen ~/.ompa/audit.pem             # Ed25519 (needs ompa[audit]); --alg hmac for stdlib
ao audit verify --vault-path ./vault [--key ~/.ompa/audit.pem.pub] [--anchor head.json]
ao audit head  --vault-path ./vault > ~/anchors/$(date +%F).json
ao audit export bundle.json --vault-path ./vault --proof 42
ao audit verify-bundle bundle.json --key audit.pem.pub
ao audit as-of 2026-10-21T08:00:00Z Kai --vault-path ./vault
ao audit log --vault-path ./vault --last 20
ao forget "Zorblatt Quince" --alias "Z. Quince" --vault-path ./vault [--dry-run]
ao retention add 30 --tag scratch ; ao retention apply [--dry-run] ; ao retention list
ao hold add "Acme" --kind subject --reason "case 42" ; ao hold release h-1234abcd
ao acl init alice --reader team:eng --team eng=bob,carol ; ao acl show

MCP tools: ao_audit_verify, ao_audit_head, ao_audit_export, ao_forget (dry run unless dry_run: false) and ao_as_of. Every tool accepts a principal argument (see the trust model). ao_search and ao_kg_query results carry citation.

docs.title: What is recorded
docs.text:
Every memory mutation appends one entry to .palace/audit.sqlite3:

action when note.write / note.edit / note.delete write(), update_brain(), export_to_shared(), import_to_personal(), delete_note() note.observed post_tool() saw an agent write/edit a note outside the API note.baseline, fact.baseline, audit.baseline enable_audit() snapshot of pre-existing data fact.add / fact.merge / fact.invalidate / fact.delete knowledge-graph mutations, including facts derived from notes forget, retention.apply erasure / expiry tombstones (list the redacted entry seqs) policy.change, acl.change, audit.export governance changes access.denied, hold.blocked, forget.blocked refused attempts (who, what, which vault) audit.genesis, audit.key chain start; signing key registration

Note entries store the path, size and SHA-256 of the note, not its text. Fact entries store the fact (subject, predicate, object, validity interval, source path/line/hash). One write() produces one audit transaction: the note entry plus every fact derived from it. That is one SQLite commit and one head update.

docs.title: Entry format
docs.text:
entry_hash = SHA-256( canonical_json({v, seq, ts, actor, action, body_hash, prev}) )
body_hash  = SHA-256( canonical_json(body + {"_salt": 128 random bits}) )
  • canonical_json = sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8.
  • prev is the previous entry's hash (64 zeros for genesis).
  • The salt makes every body commitment unguessable, so a redacted body cannot be confirmed by brute force ("was it Alice?").
  • Every checkpoint_interval entries (default 1000, fixed at genesis) a Merkle checkpoint (RFC 6962 hashing) over that range is stored and chained to the previous checkpoint. It allows O(log n) inclusion proofs in evidence bundles.
  • audit.sqlite3.head.json holds the latest {seq, hash} (signed when signing is on). It is written atomically in the same transaction as the entries, and it is how tail truncation is detected.

docs.title: Verification (verify, ao audit verify, ao_audit_verify)
docs.text:
Verification re-derives everything and reports each problem with its kind and seq:

detects how issue kind any edited field of any entry header hash, body hash hash_mismatch, body_mismatch deleted entry seq gap + broken prev link gap, prev_mismatch reordered entries prev links / hashes prev_mismatch, hash_mismatch inserted (forged) entry prev links of the next entry prev_mismatch, gap appended forged entry head file behind the chain head_stale truncated tail head file / anchors head_mismatch, anchor_mismatch deleted / emptied log refuses to start a new chain over an existing head file AuditError on open body removed without a tombstone redaction accounting unaccounted_redaction checkpoint edited / deleted checkpoint chain, Merkle root, expected boundaries checkpoint_* corrupt, cut or padded database file PRAGMA quick_check, read errors, file size vs page size and header page count db_error, db_size (with key) forged or re-hashed entries, stripped or re-keyed signatures Ed25519 / HMAC signatures on entries, checkpoints, head bad_signature, key_changed, wrong_key, head_signature

verify also reports drift: notes whose current SHA-256 differs from the last audited version (edited outside OMPA), notes never audited, and audited notes that disappeared.

Measured (tests and benchmarks/audit_tamper_mc.py): see Test results below.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text:
Protects against. Someone with write access to the vault files after the fact who wants to silently change, remove, reorder or insert history. This covers a compromised agent process, a careless script, a sync conflict, or a malicious insider who edits SQLite directly. Any such change is detected on the next verify, subject to the conditions below.

Detection depends on what the attacker lacks:

  1. Without a key and without external anchors, the attacker can rewrite the whole database and head file consistently: re-hash every entry, rebuild every checkpoint, rewrite the head. This cannot be detected from the files alone. No local-only hash chain can prevent it, and we test this limit explicitly (test_full_rehash_needs_anchor_or_key, MC mode unsigned_rehash: 0% detected without an anchor, 100% with one).
  2. External anchors defeat full rewrites. Periodically store ao audit head output somewhere the attacker cannot write: a ticket, a WORM bucket, another system's log, email to yourself. Pass the saved heads to verify --anchor. Any rewrite of history before an anchored head is detected.
  3. Signing defeats rewrites by anyone without the key. HMAC needs the verifier to hold the same secret. Ed25519 lets auditors verify with only the public key. Keep the private key off the agent's machine, or at least outside the vault, with mode 0600. An attacker who has the signing key can forge everything after the point where they obtained it. Combine signing with anchors.

Does not protect against:

  • Actions never routed through OMPA. Edits made with an editor or git pull are not logged as they happen; verify reports them as drift afterwards.
  • Lies told before logging. The log records what the agent wrote, not whether it was true.
  • Availability. An attacker can delete the vault. Deletion is detectable, not preventable.
  • Crash window. Mutations are logged after the underlying write succeeds (note file / KG commit), in a separate SQLite database. A crash between the two leaves an unlogged change. verify reports it as drift for notes; it is not reported for KG facts. A crash between the head write and the commit reports head_mismatch (a false alarm, distinguishable by inspection).
  • Key rotation within one log is not supported: a key change after the verified segment is reported as key_changed. To rotate, start a new log and anchor the old head in it.
  • Confidentiality. The log is not encrypted; protect it with filesystem permissions or disk encryption.
  • Multi-writer sync. A vault synced between machines that write concurrently forks the chain. Verify detects the fork; it is not merged.

docs.title: Identity and access control trust model
docs.text:
ACLs are enforced in the API layer (Ompa methods, the KG guard, and the MCP dispatcher). They are not an OS boundary: a process with filesystem access can read files directly. Principals are self-asserted: the principal= argument, $OMPA_PRINCIPAL, or the MCP principal field. MCP over stdio has no authentication. To pin the identity for an MCP server, set $OMPA_PRINCIPAL in the server's environment. A client-supplied principal that differs from it is then rejected (and logged). Treat ACLs as protection against accidental cross-agent or cross-team access and as an accountability record, not as a defence against a malicious local user. For hard isolation, use separate OS users or containers per vault.

Denied attempts are always logged, even when they occur inside an audit transaction that rolls back. A flood of denied requests therefore grows the log; rate-limit untrusted callers upstream.

docs.title: Provenance and citations
docs.text:
SearchResult.citation (also in MCP ao_search):

{"path": "/v/work/orion.md", "line_start": 9, "line_end": 9,
 "byte_start": 3087, "byte_end": 3160,
 "content_sha256": "…", "author": "agent-7",
 "recorded_at": "2026-10-21T07:16:35.123456Z", "recorded_source": "audit",
 "recorded_by": "agent-7", "audited_sha256": "…", "matches_audit": true,
 "valid_from": "2026-10-21", "valid_to": null, "stale": false}
  • The span is for the matched chunk (semantic) or the line containing the most query terms (keyword). Byte offsets index the raw file bytes: raw[byte_start:byte_end].
  • content_sha256 is the hash of the file as read now. matches_audit says whether that equals the last audited version. stale means the note changed after it was indexed.
  • recorded_at/recorded_by (transaction time) come from the audit log, or from the file mtime when audit is off (recorded_source: "mtime"). valid_from/valid_to (valid time) come from frontmatter (date/valid_from, valid_to/expires). author comes from frontmatter author/agent, else the recording principal.

Triple.citation (kg_query, timeline, MCP ao_kg_query): source note path, line, source content_sha256, author (agent id), recorded_at (transaction time) and valid_from/valid_to. The new KG columns (agent, source_line, source_sha256) are added in place to existing databases. Old rows have them as NULL.

docs.title: Point in time: as_of(t)
docs.text:
ao.as_of(t) replays the audit chain up to transaction time t into a temporary knowledge graph:

  • view.facts(entity, valid_at=None): facts as recorded by t. This is bitemporal: valid_at selects the valid-time instant and defaults to the date of t.
  • view.notes(): note versions (path → sha256, ts, actor) that existed at t.
  • view.stats(): entries replayed and redacted entries skipped.

t is ISO 8601; with no offset it is taken as UTC, and a bare date means the end of that day (UTC). Erased or expired data is not reconstructable by design. A redacted entry is skipped, including any other facts that shared that entry's body.

docs.title: Data policies
docs.text:
.palace/policies.json (mode 0600). Changes require admin and are logged as policy.change.

Retention: add_retention_rule(ttl_days, tag=… | folder=… | predicate=… | all=True), then apply_retention(dry_run=False) (CLI: ao retention apply). Run it from cron or CI; nothing expires automatically in the background.

  • Notes are aged by frontmatter date, else file mtime. Facts (predicate=) are aged by recorded time.
  • Expired notes are deleted together with the facts derived from them and their index entries.
  • The matching audit entry bodies are redacted, the retention.apply tombstone is appended, and all SQLite files are vacuumed.
  • Held items are skipped and reported.

Legal hold: add_legal_hold(value, kind="subject"|"path"|"tag", reason=…). A covered note cannot be deleted, overwritten, expired or erased. Blocked attempts raise LegalHoldError and are logged (hold.blocked, forget.blocked). Release with remove_policy(hold_id). Holds do not stop new notes being written.

Right to erasure: forget(subject | [subject, alias, …]). Requires admin; blocked by a covering hold. Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive; spaces, - and _ are interchangeable ("Ada Lovelace" ≈ "ada-lovelace"). It:

  1. Deletes notes named after the subject, renames paths containing it, and redacts mentions ([REDACTED]) in every other note. It also scrubs other text files in the vault, including palace.json and PreCompact session-log JSON. acl.json, policies.json and the head file are never rewritten; matches in them are reported as protected_matches.
  2. Deletes matching KG facts and entities, plus facts sourced from deleted notes, then re-derives facts for rewritten notes.
  3. Drops the affected keyword (FTS5) and semantic (vectors + excerpts) index entries.
  4. Redacts every matching audit-entry body. Hashes stay, so the chain still verifies. It then appends a forget tombstone listing the redacted seqs, with subject_commitment = SHA-256(nonce ‖ 0x00 ‖ casefold(subject)). The nonce is returned in the receipt and stored nowhere else: the requester can later prove which subject a tombstone covers, but the log alone does not reveal it.
  5. Runs VACUUM with secure_delete and truncates the WAL of every SQLite file, so no deleted bytes remain in the database files.

The tests grep every byte of every file in the vault, including .sqlite3, -wal, FTS and vector files, for the subject (case-insensitive). They expect zero hits after forget.

Not covered by erasure: copies outside the vault (backups, snapshots, git history, synced replicas, the LLM provider's logs), the agent's own context window, filesystem-level remnants (unallocated blocks, SSD wear levelling, journaling filesystems), and mentions that don't match the given names (nicknames, misspellings, pronouns). Pass every alias, and erase copies outside the vault with their own tools.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
.palace/acl.json (absent = open vault, the legacy behaviour):

{"version": 1, "owner": "alice",
 "teams": {"eng": ["alice", "bob"]},
 "read": ["team:eng"], "write": ["alice"], "admin": ["alice"]}
  • Entries are principal ids, team:<name> or *. admin ⊇ write ⊇ read.
  • A malformed file fails closed: opening the vault raises.
  • Each vault has its own ACL. In dual-vault mode, give the personal vault AccessPolicy.template(owner) (private) and the shared vault team grants.
  • set_acl() / ao acl init installs one. Once an ACL exists, changing it requires admin. Bootstrapping is unauthenticated: whoever creates the first ACL owns the vault.
  • An ACL forces audit on, because denials must be recorded.
needs read needs write needs admin search, get_brain_note, kg_query/timeline, as_of, audit_verify/head/export, policies write, update_brain, delete_note, kg_add/invalidate, kg_populate, sync, rebuild_index, post_tool (raises after the fact) forget, apply_retention, holds, retention rules, set_acl, enable_audit

docs.title: Migration (existing vaults)
docs.text:
Audit is off by default, so nothing changes for existing users. A vault is audited if Ompa(audit=True), or if it already has .palace/audit.sqlite3 (or its head file, or acl.json).

  1. Back up the vault.
  2. Run ao audit enable --vault-path VAULT [--key KEY], or call Ompa(...).enable_audit(). This creates the log and records a baseline (note.baseline per note with its SHA-256, fact.baseline per KG row). History before enabling is not reconstructable; the baseline is the audited starting state.
  3. Optional: ao audit keygen and pass --key / audit_key= (or set $OMPA_AUDIT_KEY_FILE). Enabling signing on an existing log appends an audit.key entry. Earlier entries remain covered by the chain and are reported as an unsigned prefix.
  4. Optional: ao acl init OWNER … and ao retention add ….
  5. Schedule ao audit verify plus anchor storage (e.g. daily ao audit head to an external location), and ao retention apply if you use retention.

KG schema changes are additive (three nullable columns) and happen automatically. The semantic index format is unchanged; citations are computed at query time.

docs.title: Compliance mapping
docs.text:
OMPA supports the following controls. It does not by itself satisfy them, and it is not certified under any of them.

framework requirement (paraphrased) how OMPA supports it what you still need SOC 2 (TSC CC7.2/CC7.3, CC6.1, CC8.1) monitor and log system activity, detect anomalies, logical access, change management complete mutation log with actor + time; tamper-evident chain; denial logging; per-vault ACL log review process, alerting, identity provider, auditor attestation HIPAA Security Rule §164.312(b), (c)(1), (d) audit controls; integrity of ePHI; person/entity authentication audit controls + integrity verification (hash chain, signatures) authentication (principals are self-asserted), encryption at rest/in transit, BAAs, risk analysis GDPR Art. 17 (erasure), Art. 5(1)(e) (storage limitation), Art. 30 (records), Art. 5(2) (accountability) erase personal data on request; keep no longer than necessary; demonstrate compliance forget() with a verifiable tombstone and commitment; TTL retention; evidence bundles erasure in backups and processors, lawful-basis assessment, DPIA, request handling SEC Rule 17a-4(f) / FINRA 4511 records preserved in non-rewriteable, non-erasable form or with a complete time-stamped audit trail; legal hold append-only, signed, anchorable audit trail; legal hold blocks deletion a compliant storage medium/third party (WORM or audit-trail system per 17a-4(f)(2)), designated third-party access, retention periods ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.15 (logging), A.8.10 (information deletion) produce, protect and analyse logs; delete information when no longer required protected logs; deletion with proof ISMS, log monitoring

For 17a-4 in particular: SQLite on an ordinary filesystem is not WORM storage. Ship the evidence bundles and anchors to a compliant store.

docs.text:
See benchmarks/README.md (section Audit memory) for the full method. The numbers below are copied from that run.

Measured 2026-10-21 (PT) on the shared 16 GB Linux box, Python 3.12, while another worker shared the CPU. Numbers vary run to run; compare within a table only.

Single AuditLog.append (own transaction + head update): p50 101 µs, 8131 appends/s.

Tamper Monte Carlo (benchmarks/audit_tamper_mc.py; one random tamper per trial, every 5th trial also verifies the untouched log as a false-positive control):

mode seeds trials effective tampers detected rate false positives unsigned 20261021, 7, 1337, 42, 99 25,000 24,998 24,998 1.0000 0/5,000 hmac 20261021, 7, 1337, 42, 99 25,000 25,000 25,000 1.0000 0/5,000 unsigned_rehash 20261021, 7, 1337 1,500 1,500 0 0.0000 0/300 unsigned_rehash + external anchor 20261021, 7, 1337 1,500 1,500 1,500 1.0000 —

Interpretation:

  • Audit adds about 0.5 ms per keyword-only write (unsigned), 0.6 ms with HMAC and 0.8 ms with Ed25519. Most of this is the atomic head-file replace plus ~7 chain entries per write (the note and every fact derived from it). With semantic indexing on, writes are dominated by embedding.
  • A standalone kg_add goes from ~40 µs to ~200 µs because each call is its own audited transaction. Batch with ao.gov.txn() (one head update per batch) when bulk loading.
  • Verify is linear: ~7–9 µs/entry unsigned/HMAC (0.77 s / 0.92 s at 100k) and ~100 µs/entry with Ed25519 (~10 s at 100k). Storage is ~550–650 B/entry.
  • Citations add ~0.2 ms per search. Pass citations=False to skip them.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide walks you from zero to a running OMPA vault in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install ompa          # Core only (vault + palace + KG + CLI + MCP)
pip install ompa[all]     # Adds local semantic search (sentence-transformers)

Requires Python 3.10+.

docs.title: Initialize a vault
docs.text:
Navigate to your project directory and run:

ao init

This creates the vault structure:

./
├── brain/        # Persistent agent memory: North Star, active work, people
├── work/         # Project work: decisions, incidents, wins, features
├── org/          # Organization: people, teams, processes
├── perf/         # Performance: retros, reviews, blockers
└── .palace/      # Agent metadata: wings, rooms, KG database, semantic index

Verify with:

ao status
ao doctor      # Full health check

docs.title: CLI workflow
docs.text:
# At session start — inject ~2K tokens of context
ao session-start

# Route a message to the right vault folder
ao classify "We decided to go with Postgres over MySQL"
# → MessageType.DECISION → work/decisions/...

# Semantic search (zero API cost)
ao search "database decisions"

# Query the knowledge graph
ao kg-query "Postgres"

# End of session
ao wrap-up

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from ompa import Ompa

ao = Ompa(vault_path="./workspace")

# Session start — returns ~2K token context string
context = ao.session_start()
print(context.output)  # inject this into your agent's system prompt

# Handle a user message
ao.handle_message("We're switching to Postgres for the main DB")

# After a tool call
ao.post_tool("write", {"file_path": "work/decisions/postgres.md"})

# Semantic search
results = ao.search("authentication decisions")
for r in results:
    print(f"{r.score:.2f}  {r.path}")

# Knowledge graph
ao.kg.add_triple("Kai", "works_on", "auth-service", valid_from="2026-01-01")
facts = ao.kg.query_entity("Kai")

# End session
ao.stop()

docs.title: MCP server (Claude Desktop / Cursor)
docs.text:
Add OMPA as an MCP server so Claude can access your vault directly:

claude mcp add ompa -- python -m ompa.mcp_server

Then restart Claude Desktop. You'll see 15 new tools: ao_session_start, ao_search, ao_classify, etc.

See the MCP Server guide for full setup instructions.

docs.title: Semantic search
docs.text:
Semantic search is optional and uses sentence-transformers locally — no OpenAI/Anthropic API calls.

pip install ompa[all]       # Install with semantic support
ao rebuild-index            # Build the index from your vault
ao search "your query"      # Now uses semantic similarity

docs.title: Why OMPA vs raw Obsidian?
docs.text: One page for consulting leads. OMPA is the installable agent-memory layer that turns an Obsidian-style markdown vault into durable, queryable memory for any AI agent — without lock-in to a single IDE or paid embedding API.

docs.title: The consulting problem
docs.text:
Teams already dump decisions into Obsidian (or a shared markdown vault). That works for humans. It fails for agents:

Pain What raw Obsidian gives you What agents need Lost decisions across sessions Notes in folders Lifecycle hooks that inject ~2K tokens of relevant memory at session start Expensive context windows Manual copy/paste Token-budgeted hooks (~100–200 per turn) “Search” that bleeds money Embeddings + vector DB Local semantic search (or Locus vectorless RAG) No provenance Wikilinks humans follow Temporal knowledge graph + explainable retrieval Framework lock-in Plugins for one app Python API + MCP — Claude Code, Cursor, LangChain, custom agents

OMPA is the productized answer: pip install ompa → vault + palace + temporal KG in one package.

docs.title: What you get in one install
docs.text:
Vault (human markdown)  →  Palace (agent metadata)  →  Temporal KG (SQLite facts)
  • Vault — brain / work / org / perf layout; every significant event as markdown humans can audit
  • Palace — wings → rooms → drawers, halls, tunnels — agent-navigable structure over the vault
  • Knowledge graph — subject → predicate → object with validity windows; query “what was true when?”
  • 15 MCP tools + CLI (ao) — drop into Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP host
  • Dual-vault isolation — shared team vault vs personal notes without leaking identifiers

Benchmark signal: on the full LongMemEval-S (n=470), OMPA's own measured R@5 is 0.979 with hybrid search and 0.970 with keyword-only search. Storage is verbatim, and local search has no per-query API cost. See benchmarks/README.md.

pip install ompa
ao init && ao session-start

docs.title: Why not “just Obsidian”?
docs.text:
Raw Obsidian is an excellent human second brain. It is not an agent memory runtime:

  1. No session contract — agents do not get a budgeted session_start / wrap-up lifecycle
  2. No typed routing — OMPA auto-classifies 15 message types (DECISION, INCIDENT, WIN, …) into the right folders
  3. No temporal facts — Obsidian links are spatial; OMPA’s KG tracks when a fact was valid
  4. No MCP surface — consultants can wire memory into client agents in minutes, not weeks of plugin glue
  5. No dual-vault hygiene — team vs personal isolation is a first-class config, not a folder convention

Keep Obsidian (or any markdown editor) for humans. Put OMPA underneath so agents write and recall the same corpus safely.

docs.title: Companion stack (retrieval + compliance)

OMPA is the memory schema and temporal KG. Pair it with:

Piece Repo Role OMPA jmiaie/ompa · PyPI Vault + palace + temporal KG; agent lifecycle + MCP Locus jmiaie/locus · PyPI locus-rag Vectorless RAG (BM25 + KG + link walking); explainable retrieval, zero GPU CognitionOS jmiaie/cognition-os Compliance-grade composition — audit, RBAC, retention, PHI redaction on top of Locus + OMPA

Pitch in one sentence: install OMPA for agent memory; add Locus when you need defensible “why this result”; bring CognitionOS when regulated clients need audit trails.

Agents / MCP hosts

docs.title: ompa.knowledge_graph.KnowledgeGraph
docs.text:
Source code in ompa/knowledge_graph.py 
class KnowledgeGraph:
    def __init__(self, db_path: str = None):
        self.db_path = Path(db_path or DEFAULT_KG_PATH).expanduser()
        self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._local = threading.local()  # per-thread connection cache
        # Optional governance hooks, wired by Ompa when audit/ACL are enabled:
        #   audit: ompa.audit.AuditLog -- every mutation is appended to the chain
        #   guard: callable(op: "read"|"write") raising AccessDeniedError
        #   agent: author/agent id stamped on new facts (provenance)
        self.audit = None
        self.guard = None
        self.agent: str | None = None
        self._init_db()

    def _get_connection(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        """Return a thread-local connection, creating one if needed."""
        if not getattr(self._local, "conn", None):
            conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.db_path), check_same_thread=False)
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            # WAL mode: readers don't block writers; writers don't block readers.
            # Persists in the db file — only needed once, idempotent thereafter.
            conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            # NORMAL is safe with WAL and significantly faster than FULL.
            conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
            self._local.conn = conn
        return self._local.conn

    @contextmanager
    def _conn(self):
        """Yield the thread-local connection for a single transaction."""
        conn = self._get_connection()
        try:
            yield conn
            conn.commit()
        except Exception:
            conn.rollback()
            raise

    def _init_db(self) -> None:
        """Initialize the database schema and indexes."""
        with self._conn() as conn:
            conn.executescript("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    name TEXT NOT NULL,
                    type TEXT DEFAULT 'unknown',
                    created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                );

                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS triples (
                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    subject TEXT NOT NULL,
                    predicate TEXT NOT NULL,
                    object TEXT NOT NULL,
                    valid_from TEXT,
                    valid_to TEXT,
                    confidence REAL DEFAULT 1.0,
                    source_file TEXT,
                    extracted_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                );

                -- Basic lookup indexes
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_subject   ON triples(subject);
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_predicate ON triples(predicate);
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_object    ON triples(object);

                -- Composite indexes for timeline queries and reverse lookups
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_subject_date
                    ON triples(subject, valid_from);
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_object_pred
                    ON triples(object, predicate);
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_validity
                    ON triples(valid_from, valid_to);

                -- Exact-fact lookup for add_triple's overlap check.  Without it
                -- each write scans every row sharing the subject or the
                -- (object, predicate) pair, i.e. O(fan-out) per insert.
                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_triples_spo
                    ON triples(subject, predicate, object);
            """)
            # Provenance columns (added in place on pre-existing databases).
            have = {r[1] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(triples)")}
            for col, decl in (
                ("agent", "TEXT"),
                ("source_line", "INTEGER"),
                ("source_sha256", "TEXT"),
            ):
                if col not in have:
                    conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE triples ADD COLUMN {col} {decl}")  # nosec B608

    def _entity_id(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Generate a stable ID for an entity."""
        return _entity_id(name)

    def _interval_id(self, subject: str, predicate: str, obj: str, valid_from: str | None) -> str:
        """Stable ID for one validity interval of a fact."""
        key = f"{subject}|{predicate}|{obj}|{valid_from or ''}"
        return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

    def _now(self) -> str:
        return datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    def _check(self, op: str) -> None:
        if self.guard is not None:
            self.guard(op)

    def _log(self, action: str, body: dict) -> None:
        if self.audit is not None:
            self.audit.append(action, body, actor=self.agent)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Entity operations
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def add_entity(self, name: str, entity_type: str = "unknown") -> None:
        """Add an entity."""
        entity_id = self._entity_id(name)
        with self._conn() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO entities (id, name, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                (entity_id, name, entity_type),
            )

    def query_entity(self, name: str, as_of: str = None) -> list[Triple]:
        """
        Query all current triples for an entity.

        Args:
            name: Entity name
            as_of: YYYY-MM-DD date for historical query. Defaults to today.
        """
        as_of = as_of or self._now()

        # Filter in SQL for performance
        query = (
            f"SELECT {_TRIPLE_COLS} FROM triples "  # nosec B608 - constant column list
            "WHERE (subject = ? OR object = ?)"
            " AND (valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= ?)"
            " AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)"
            " ORDER BY valid_from DESC"
        )
        self._check("read")
        with self._conn() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(query, (name, name, as_of, as_of)).fetchall()

        return [_row_to_triple(row) for row in rows]

    def query_relation(self, subject: str, predicate: str) -> list[Triple]:
        """Query all triples matching a specific subject+predicate."""
        self._check("read")
        with self._conn() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                f"SELECT {_TRIPLE_COLS} FROM triples WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ?",  # nosec B608
                (subject, predicate),
            ).fetchall()
        return [_row_to_triple(r) for r in rows]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Triple operations
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def add_triple(
        self,
        subject: str,
        predicate: str,
        object: str,
        valid_from: str = None,
        valid_to: str = None,
        confidence: float = 1.0,
        source: str = None,
        source_line: int | None = None,
        source_sha256: str | None = None,
        agent: str | None = None,
        recorded_at: str | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Add a fact triple to the knowledge graph.

        Args:
            subject: Subject entity (e.g., "Kai")
            predicate: Relationship (e.g., "works_on", "completed", "recommended")
            object: Object entity (e.g., "Orion")
            valid_from: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). None = always true.
            valid_to: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). None = still true.
            confidence: Confidence 0-1. Default 1.0.
            source: Source file or drawer reference.
            source_line: 1-based line in ``source`` the fact was extracted from.
            source_sha256: SHA-256 of the source content at extraction time.
            agent: Author/agent id (defaults to ``self.agent``).
            recorded_at: Override the recorded (transaction) time; used by
                point-in-time replay.  Defaults to now.

        Returns ``"add"`` (new interval) or ``"merge"`` (merged into an
        overlapping interval).  With auditing enabled the mutation is appended
        to the audit chain as ``fact.add`` / ``fact.merge``.
        """
        self._check("write")
        valid_from = valid_from or self._now()
        agent = agent or self.agent
        subject_id = self._entity_id(subject)
        object_id = self._entity_id(object)
        interval_id = self._interval_id(subject, predicate, object, valid_from)

        with self._conn() as conn:
            # The first statement is a write, so this (deferred) transaction holds
            # SQLite's write lock from here to commit: the check-then-write below
            # is serialized across threads and processes without BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO entities (id, name, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?), (?, ?, ?)",
                (subject_id, subject, "unknown", object_id, object, "unknown"),
            )
            # Fast path (the common case): no overlapping interval for this exact
            # fact -> append a new row.  Indexed point lookup, no merge logic.
            overlap = conn.execute(
                """SELECT 1 FROM triples
                   WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ?
                     AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)
                     AND (? IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= ?)
                   LIMIT 1""",
                (subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, valid_to),
            ).fetchone()
            if overlap is None:
                conn.execute(
                    """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO triples
                       (id, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence,
                        source_file, agent, source_line, source_sha256, extracted_at)
                       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?,
                               COALESCE(?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP))""",
                    (
                        interval_id,
                        subject,
                        predicate,
                        object,
                        valid_from,
                        valid_to,
                        confidence,
                        source,
                        agent,
                        source_line,
                        source_sha256,
                        recorded_at,
                    ),
                )
                outcome = "add"
            else:
                # Slow path: overlaps an existing interval (re-assertion) -> merge.
                self._upsert_interval(
                    conn, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, source
                )
                if source_line is not None or source_sha256 is not None or agent:
                    conn.execute(
                        """UPDATE triples SET agent = COALESCE(?, agent),
                               source_line = COALESCE(?, source_line),
                               source_sha256 = COALESCE(?, source_sha256)
                           WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ?
                             AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)
                             AND (valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= COALESCE(?, valid_from))""",
                        (
                            agent,
                            source_line,
                            source_sha256,
                            subject,
                            predicate,
                            object,
                            valid_from,
                            valid_to,
                        ),
                    )
                outcome = "merge"
        if self.audit is not None:
            self._log(
                "fact." + outcome,
                {
                    "s": subject,
                    "p": predicate,
                    "o": object,
                    "valid_from": valid_from,
                    "valid_to": valid_to,
                    "confidence": confidence,
                    "source": source,
                    "source_line": source_line,
                    "source_sha256": source_sha256,
                },
            )
        return outcome

    def _upsert_interval(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        subject: str,
        predicate: str,
        obj: str,
        valid_from: str,
        valid_to: str | None,
        confidence: float,
        source: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Record that (subject, predicate, obj) holds over [valid_from, valid_to].

        Validity history is append-only: each (subject, predicate, object) can
        have many rows, one per validity interval.  Re-asserting a fact that was
        invalidated earlier opens a *new* interval instead of overwriting the old
        one, so point-in-time queries for the earlier period stay correct.
        An assertion that overlaps existing interval(s) for the same fact is
        merged with them (interval union), which keeps repeated assertions of a
        still-true fact idempotent.
        """
        # Inclusive overlap test; NULL valid_to means "still true" (+infinity)
        rows = conn.execute(
            """SELECT id, valid_from, valid_to FROM triples
               WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ?
                 AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)
                 AND (? IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= ?)
               ORDER BY valid_from""",
            (subject, predicate, obj, valid_from, valid_to, valid_to),
        ).fetchall()

        if not rows:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO triples
                   (id, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, source_file)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (
                    self._interval_id(subject, predicate, obj, valid_from),
                    subject,
                    predicate,
                    obj,
                    valid_from,
                    valid_to,
                    confidence,
                    source,
                ),
            )
            return

        starts = [valid_from] + [r["valid_from"] for r in rows]
        merged_from = None if any(v is None for v in starts) else min(starts)
        ends = [valid_to] + [r["valid_to"] for r in rows]
        merged_to = None if any(v is None for v in ends) else max(ends)

        keep_id = rows[0]["id"]
        for r in rows[1:]:
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM triples WHERE id = ?", (r["id"],))
        conn.execute(
            """UPDATE triples
               SET valid_from = ?, valid_to = ?, confidence = ?,
                   source_file = COALESCE(?, source_file)
               WHERE id = ?""",
            (merged_from, merged_to, confidence, source, keep_id),
        )

    def invalidate(self, subject: str, predicate: str, obj: str, ended: str = None) -> int:
        """
        Invalidate a triple by setting its valid_to date.
        The fact is no longer current but remains queryable historically.
        Returns the number of open intervals closed.
        """
        self._check("write")
        ended = ended or self._now()
        with self._conn() as conn:
            n = conn.execute(
                """UPDATE triples SET valid_to = ?
                   WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ? AND valid_to IS NULL""",
                (ended, subject, predicate, obj),
            ).rowcount
        if self.audit is not None:
            self._log(
                "fact.invalidate",
                {"s": subject, "p": predicate, "o": obj, "ended": ended, "rows": n},
            )
        return n

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Deletion (used by retention / erasure / note deletion; callers audit)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def find_ids(self, where: str, args: tuple = ()) -> list[str]:
        """Ids of triples matching a trusted SQL ``where`` fragment (internal use)."""
        with self._conn() as conn:
            return [
                r[0]
                for r in conn.execute(f"SELECT id FROM triples WHERE {where}", args)  # nosec B608
            ]

    def delete_ids(self, ids: list[str]) -> int:
        """Hard-delete triples by id.  Caller is responsible for auditing."""
        if not ids:
            return 0
        n = 0
        with self._conn() as conn:
            for i in range(0, len(ids), 500):
                chunk = ids[i : i + 500]
                marks = ",".join("?" * len(chunk))
                n += conn.execute(
                    f"DELETE FROM triples WHERE id IN ({marks})",  # nosec B608
                    chunk,
                ).rowcount
        return n

    def delete_entities(self, names: list[str]) -> int:
        """Remove entity rows (no longer referenced by any triple)."""
        n = 0
        with self._conn() as conn:
            for name in names:
                n += conn.execute(
                    """DELETE FROM entities WHERE name = ? AND NOT EXISTS
                       (SELECT 1 FROM triples WHERE subject = ? OR object = ?)""",
                    (name, name, name),
                ).rowcount
        return n

    def compact(self) -> None:
        """VACUUM + truncate the WAL so deleted rows leave no recoverable bytes."""
        conn = self._get_connection()
        conn.commit()
        conn.execute("PRAGMA secure_delete=ON")
        conn.execute("VACUUM")
        conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)")

    def close(self) -> None:
        conn = getattr(self._local, "conn", None)
        if conn is not None:
            conn.close()
            self._local.conn = None

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Timeline
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def timeline(self, entity: str) -> list[dict]:
        """
        Get the chronological story of an entity.
        Returns all triples ordered by valid_from with direction indicators.
        """
        self._check("read")
        with self._conn() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                """SELECT subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, source_file,
                          source_line, source_sha256, agent, extracted_at
                   FROM triples
                   WHERE subject = ? OR object = ?
                   ORDER BY valid_from ASC NULLS FIRST""",

                note_name,
                "created_on",

def add_triple(
    self,
    subject: str,
    predicate: str,
    object: str,
    valid_from: str = None,
    valid_to: str = None,
    confidence: float = 1.0,
    source: str = None,
    source_line: int | None = None,
    source_sha256: str | None = None,
    agent: str | None = None,
    recorded_at: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Add a fact triple to the knowledge graph.

    Args:
        subject: Subject entity (e.g., "Kai")
        predicate: Relationship (e.g., "works_on", "completed", "recommended")
        object: Object entity (e.g., "Orion")
        valid_from: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). None = always true.
        valid_to: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). None = still true.
        confidence: Confidence 0-1. Default 1.0.
        source: Source file or drawer reference.
        source_line: 1-based line in ``source`` the fact was extracted from.
        source_sha256: SHA-256 of the source content at extraction time.
        agent: Author/agent id (defaults to ``self.agent``).
        recorded_at: Override the recorded (transaction) time; used by
            point-in-time replay.  Defaults to now.

    Returns ``"add"`` (new interval) or ``"merge"`` (merged into an
    overlapping interval).  With auditing enabled the mutation is appended
    to the audit chain as ``fact.add`` / ``fact.merge``.
    """
    self._check("write")
    valid_from = valid_from or self._now()
    agent = agent or self.agent
    subject_id = self._entity_id(subject)
    object_id = self._entity_id(object)
    interval_id = self._interval_id(subject, predicate, object, valid_from)

    with self._conn() as conn:
        # The first statement is a write, so this (deferred) transaction holds
        # SQLite's write lock from here to commit: the check-then-write below
        # is serialized across threads and processes without BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO entities (id, name, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?), (?, ?, ?)",
            (subject_id, subject, "unknown", object_id, object, "unknown"),
        )
        # Fast path (the common case): no overlapping interval for this exact
        # fact -> append a new row.  Indexed point lookup, no merge logic.
        overlap = conn.execute(
            """SELECT 1 FROM triples
               WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ?
                 AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)
                 AND (? IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= ?)
               LIMIT 1""",
            (subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, valid_to),
        ).fetchone()
        if overlap is None:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR REPLACE INTO triples
                   (id, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence,
                    source_file, agent, source_line, source_sha256, extracted_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?,
                           COALESCE(?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP))""",
                (
                    interval_id,
                    subject,
                    predicate,
                    object,
                    valid_from,
                    valid_to,
                    confidence,
                    source,
                    agent,
                    source_line,
                    source_sha256,
                    recorded_at,
                ),
            )
            outcome = "add"
        else:
            # Slow path: overlaps an existing interval (re-assertion) -> merge.
            self._upsert_interval(
                conn, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, source
            )
            if source_line is not None or source_sha256 is not None or agent:
                conn.execute(
                    """UPDATE triples SET agent = COALESCE(?, agent),
                           source_line = COALESCE(?, source_line),
                           source_sha256 = COALESCE(?, source_sha256)
                       WHERE subject = ? AND predicate = ? AND object = ?
                         AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= ?)
                         AND (valid_from IS NULL OR valid_from <= COALESCE(?, valid_from))""",
                    (
                        agent,
                        source_line,
                        source_sha256,
                        subject,
                        predicate,
                        object,
                        valid_from,
                        valid_to,
                    ),
                )
            outcome = "merge"
    if self.audit is not None:
        self._log(
            "fact." + outcome,
            {
                "s": subject,
                "p": predicate,
                "o": object,
                "valid_from": valid_from,
                "valid_to": valid_to,
                "confidence": confidence,
                "source": source,
                "source_line": source_line,
                "source_sha256": source_sha256,
            },
        )
    return outcome

                    "author": row["agent"],
                    "recorded_at": row["extracted_at"],
                    "valid_from": row["valid_from"],
                    "valid_to": row["valid_to"],
                },
            }
        )
    return timeline

class Ompa:
    """
    Universal agent memory layer.

    Integrates:
    - Vault (obsidian-mind conventions: brain/work/org/perf folders, wikilinks)
    - Palace (MemPalace wings/rooms/closets/drawers metadata layer)
    - Knowledge Graph (temporal SQLite triples with validity windows)
    - Hooks (session_start, user_message, post_tool, pre_compact, stop)
    - Classifier (15 message types with routing hints)
    - Semantic Search (local sentence-transformers)

    Usage (single vault — legacy):
        ao = Ompa(vault_path="./workspace")

    Usage (dual vault):
        ao = Ompa(
            shared_vault_path="/shared/ompa-vault",
            personal_vault_path="~/.ompa-personal",
            isolation_mode="strict",
        )
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        vault_path: str | Path = None,
        agent_name: str = "agent",
        enable_semantic: bool = True,
        embedding_backend=None,  # EmbeddingBackend protocol — e.g. NIMEmbeddingBackend
        # Dual-vault parameters
        shared_vault_path: str | Path = None,
        personal_vault_path: str | Path = None,
        isolation_mode: str = "strict",
        index_refresh_interval: float = 1.0,
        # Audit memory (see docs/AUDIT.md)
        principal: str | None = None,
        audit: bool | None = None,
        audit_key=None,
    ):
        """
        Audit-memory args:
            principal: user/agent/team id this instance acts as (ACL checks,
                audit actor, fact provenance).  Default: $OMPA_PRINCIPAL, else
                ``agent_name``.  Self-asserted: see docs/AUDIT.md threat model.
            audit: True = enable the hash-chained audit log (created + baseline
                on first use); False = off; None (default) = on iff the vault
                already has ``.palace/audit.sqlite3`` or ``.palace/acl.json``.
            audit_key: signer for entries/checkpoints: a key-file path
                (Ed25519 PEM needs the ``audit`` extra; otherwise an HMAC key)
                or a signer object.  Default: $OMPA_AUDIT_KEY_FILE if set.
        """
        self.agent_name = agent_name
        self._enable_semantic = enable_semantic
        # Seconds between automatic staleness checks of the semantic index on
        # search (0 = check on every search).  Writes through Ompa.write() are
        # indexed immediately regardless; this catches edits made outside OMPA.
        self.index_refresh_interval = index_refresh_interval
        self._last_refresh: dict[tuple[int, int], float] = {}
        self._embedding_backend = embedding_backend  # optional custom backend
        self._session_started = False
        self._last_classification: Classification | None = None

        # Dual-vault config
        self.dual_config = DualVaultConfig(
            isolation_mode=IsolationMode(isolation_mode),
        )

        if shared_vault_path and personal_vault_path:
            # Dual-vault mode
            self.dual_config.shared_path = Path(shared_vault_path).expanduser()
            self.dual_config.personal_path = Path(personal_vault_path).expanduser()
            self.vault_path = self.dual_config.shared_path  # primary for hooks

            # Shared vault systems
            self.vault = Vault(self.dual_config.shared_path)
            self.palace = Palace(self.dual_config.shared_path / ".palace")
            self.kg = KnowledgeGraph(
                db_path=str(self.dual_config.shared_path / ".palace" / "knowledge_graph.sqlite3")
            )

            # Personal vault systems
            self.personal_vault = Vault(self.dual_config.personal_path)
            self.personal_palace = Palace(self.dual_config.personal_path / ".palace")
            self.personal_kg = KnowledgeGraph(
                db_path=str(self.dual_config.personal_path / ".palace" / "knowledge_graph.sqlite3")
            )
        else:
            # Single-vault mode (legacy / backward compatible)
            self.vault_path = Path(vault_path or ".")
            self.vault = Vault(self.vault_path)
            self.palace = Palace(self.vault_path / ".palace")
            self.kg = KnowledgeGraph(
                db_path=str(self.vault_path / ".palace" / "knowledge_graph.sqlite3")
            )
            self.personal_vault = None
            self.personal_palace = None
            self.personal_kg = None

        # Governance: audit chain + ACL + data policies, one context per vault
        self.principal = principal or os.environ.get("OMPA_PRINCIPAL") or agent_name
        signer = self._resolve_signer(audit_key)
        self._signer = signer
        self.gov = VaultGovernance(self.vault_path, self.principal, audit, signer, "shared")
        self.personal_gov: VaultGovernance | None = None
        if self.personal_kg is not None:
            self.personal_gov = VaultGovernance(
                self.dual_config.personal_path, self.principal, audit, signer, "personal"
            )
        for gov, kg in ((self.gov, self.kg), (self.personal_gov, self.personal_kg)):
            if gov is None:
                continue
            self._wire_kg(kg, gov)
            if gov.created:
                gov.baseline(kg)

        self.classifier = MessageClassifier()
        self.hooks = HookManager(self.vault_path, agent_name=self.agent_name)

        # Semantic search (lazy-loaded); annotated explicitly to help mypy
        self._semantic: SemanticIndex | None = None
        self._personal_semantic: SemanticIndex | None = None
        # BM25 keyword index over note content (stdlib SQLite FTS5; always on)
        self._keyword: KeywordIndex | None = None
        self._personal_keyword: KeywordIndex | None = None

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Governance plumbing
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_signer(audit_key):
        if audit_key is None:
            env = os.environ.get("OMPA_AUDIT_KEY_FILE")
            audit_key = env or None
        if audit_key is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(audit_key, str | Path):
            from .audit import load_key

            return load_key(audit_key)
        return audit_key

    def _wire_kg(self, kg: KnowledgeGraph, gov: VaultGovernance) -> None:
        kg.audit = gov.audit
        kg.guard = gov.kg_guard if gov.acl is not None else None
        kg.agent = self.principal

    def _ctx(self, vault: str = "shared"):
        """(gov, kg, keyword, semantic attribute name, vault path) for a vault name."""
        if vault == "personal":
            if self.personal_gov is None:
                raise ValueError("no personal vault (not in dual-vault mode)")
            return (
                self.personal_gov,
                self.personal_kg,
                self.personal_keyword,
                "_personal_semantic",
                self.dual_config.personal_path,
            )
        if vault != "shared":
            raise ValueError(f"unknown vault {vault!r}")
        return self.gov, self.kg, self.keyword, "_semantic", self.vault_path

    def _govs(self, vaults: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:
        names = vaults or (["shared", "personal"] if self.personal_gov else ["shared"])
        return [n for n in names if n == "shared" or self.personal_gov is not None]

    @property
    def is_dual_vault(self) -> bool:
        """True if dual-vault mode is active."""
        return self.dual_config.is_dual_vault

    @property
    def keyword(self) -> KeywordIndex:
        """Lazy-open the BM25 keyword index (kept fresh by search/write)."""
        if self._keyword is None:
            self._keyword = KeywordIndex(self.vault_path / ".palace" / "keyword_index.sqlite3")
        return self._keyword

    @property
    def personal_keyword(self) -> KeywordIndex | None:
        """Lazy-open the personal vault's keyword index (dual-vault mode only)."""
        if self._personal_keyword is None and self.dual_config.personal_path:
            self._personal_keyword = KeywordIndex(
                self.dual_config.personal_path / ".palace" / "keyword_index.sqlite3"
            )
        return self._personal_keyword

    @property
    def semantic(self) -> SemanticIndex | None:
        """Lazy-load semantic index on first access."""
        if self._semantic is None and self._enable_semantic:
            self._semantic = SemanticIndex(
                index_path=self.vault_path / ".palace" / "semantic_index",
                embedding_backend=self._embedding_backend,
                keyword_index=self.keyword,
            )
            if not self._semantic.load_index():
                count = self._semantic.index_vault(self.vault_path)
                if count > 0:
                    self._semantic.save_index()
        return self._semantic

    @property
    def personal_semantic(self) -> SemanticIndex | None:
        """Lazy-load personal semantic index."""
        if (
            self._personal_semantic is None
            and self._enable_semantic
            and self.dual_config.personal_path
        ):
            self._personal_semantic = SemanticIndex(
                index_path=self.dual_config.personal_path / ".palace" / "semantic_index",
                embedding_backend=self._embedding_backend,
                keyword_index=self.personal_keyword,
            )
            if not self._personal_semantic.load_index():
                count = self._personal_semantic.index_vault(self.dual_config.personal_path)
                if count > 0:
                    self._personal_semantic.save_index()
        return self._personal_semantic

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Lifecycle Hooks
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def session_start(self) -> HookResult:
        """
        Run session start hook.
        Loads ~2K tokens: vault listing, North Star, active work, palace wings, KG stats.
        Auto-populates KG from vault if empty. Builds semantic index if missing.
        """
        # Auto-populate KG if empty
        try:
            kg_stats = self.kg.stats()
            if kg_stats["triple_count"] == 0:
                with self.gov.txn():
                    count = self.kg.populate_from_vault(self.vault_path)
                logger.info("Auto-populated KG with %d triples on session start", count)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("KG auto-population skipped: %s", e)

        # Trigger semantic index build if needed (lazy property handles this)
        if self._enable_semantic:
            try:
                _ = self.semantic  # triggers lazy build
            except Exception as e:
                logger.debug("Semantic index build skipped: %s", e)

        result = self.hooks.run_session_start(self)
        self._session_started = True
        return result

    def handle_message(self, message: str) -> HookResult:
        """
        Handle a user message.
        Classifies the message and returns routing hints (~100 tokens).
        """
        result = self.hooks.run_user_message(message, self)
        if result.success:
            self._last_classification = self.classifier.classify(message)
        return result

    def post_tool(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> HookResult:
        """
        Run post-tool hook after tool use.
        Validates writes, auto-adds to palace, updates KG + search index.
        """
        result = self.hooks.run_post_tool(tool_name, tool_input, self)

        # Auto-update on file writes
        if tool_name in ("write", "edit", "create_file"):
            file_path = tool_input.get("file_path") or tool_input.get("path")
            if file_path:
                path = Path(file_path)
                # Raises AccessDeniedError (logged) if this principal may not write here
                self.gov.require("write", "post_tool:" + tool_name, path)
                self._auto_add_to_palace(file_path)
                with self.gov.txn():
                    self._auto_update_kg(path)
                    if self.gov.audit is not None and path.suffix == ".md" and path.exists():
                        self.gov.log_note("note.observed", path, {"tool": tool_name})
                self._auto_update_index(path)

        return result

    def pre_compact(self, transcript: str) -> HookResult:
        """Run pre-compact hook before context compaction."""
        return self.hooks.run_pre_compact(transcript, self)

    def stop(self) -> HookResult:
        """Run stop hook (wrap-up checklist)."""
        result = self.hooks.run_stop(self)
        for sem in (self._semantic, self._personal_semantic):
            if sem is not None:
                try:
                    sem.flush()
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.debug("Semantic index flush failed: %s", e)
        self._session_started = False
        return result

    def wrap_up(self) -> HookResult:
        """Alias for stop()."""
        return self.stop()

    def standup(self) -> HookResult:
        """Alias for session_start()."""
        return self.session_start()

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Auto palace population
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _auto_add_to_palace(self, file_path: str) -> None:
        """Auto-add a written file to the palace metadata layer."""
        path = Path(file_path)
        if path.suffix != ".md":
            return

        try:
            # Determine wing and room from path
            parts = path.parts
            if "brain" in parts:
                wing = "brain"
                room = path.stem.lower().replace(" ", "-")
            elif "work" in parts:
                wing = "work"
                room = path.stem.lower().replace(" ", "-")
            elif "org" in parts and "people" in parts:
                wing = path.stem  # person name
                room = "context"
            else:
                return

            self.palace.create_room(wing, room)
            self.palace.link_drawer(wing, room, str(path))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Palace auto-add failed for %s: %s", file_path, e)

    def _auto_update_kg(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Auto-update knowledge graph when a note is written/edited."""
        if path.suffix != ".md":
            return
        try:
            added = self.kg.populate_from_note(path, self.vault_path)
            if added > 0:
                logger.debug("KG updated: %d triples from %s", added, path.name)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("KG auto-update failed for %s: %s", path, e)

    def _auto_update_index(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Incrementally update the search indexes when a note is written/edited."""
        if path.suffix != ".md":
            return
        try:
            self.keyword.update_file(_index_key(self.vault_path, path))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Keyword index update failed for %s: %s", path, e)
        if not self._enable_semantic:
            return
        try:
            if self._semantic is not None:
                self._semantic.update_file(path)
                logger.debug("Search index updated for %s", path.name)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Index auto-update failed for %s: %s", path, e)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Classification
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def classify(self, message: str) -> Classification:
        """Classify a user message."""
        return self.classifier.classify(message)

    def get_routing_hint(self, message: str) -> str:
        """Get a one-line routing hint for a message."""
        return self.classifier.get_routing_hint(message)

    @property
    def last_classification(self) -> Classification | None:
        """Get the last classification result."""
        return self._last_classification

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Search
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def search(
        self,
        query: str,
        limit: int = 5,
        hybrid: bool = True,
        wing: str = None,
        room: str = None,
        vaults: list[str] = None,
        citations: bool = True,
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """
        Search the vault(s) semantically.

        Args:
            query: Search query
            limit: Max results
            hybrid: Use hybrid (semantic + keyword) search
            wing: Filter by palace wing
            room: Filter by palace room
            vaults: Which vaults to search. Options: ["shared"], ["personal"],
                    ["shared", "personal"]. Default: ["shared"] in dual mode,
                    or the single vault in legacy mode.
            citations: attach a provenance ``citation`` to each result (path,
                    line/byte span, content_sha256, author, recorded_at,
                    valid_from/valid_to; see ompa.provenance).

        Raises AccessDeniedError (logged to the audit chain) if the principal
        may not read a requested vault.
        """
        # Determine which vaults to search
        if not self.is_dual_vault:
            vaults = ["shared"]  # single vault acts as shared
        elif vaults is None:
            vaults = ["shared"]
        for name in vaults:
            if name == "shared":
                self.gov.require("read", "search")
            elif name == "personal" and self.personal_gov is not None:
                self.personal_gov.require("read", "search")

        all_results = []

        # Search shared vault
        if "shared" in vaults:
            all_results.extend(
                self._search_vault(
                    self.vault, self.semantic, query, limit, hybrid, wing, room, self.keyword
                )
            )

        # Search personal vault
        if "personal" in vaults and self.personal_vault:
            personal_results = self._search_vault(
                self.personal_vault,
                self.personal_semantic,
                query,
                limit,
                hybrid,
                wing,
                room,
                self.personal_keyword,
            )
            # Tag personal results
            for r in personal_results:
                r.match_type = f"personal:{r.match_type}"
            all_results.extend(personal_results)

        # Sort by score and limit
        all_results.sort(key=lambda r: r.score, reverse=True)
        results = all_results[:limit]
        if citations:
            for r in results:
                self._attach_citation(r, query)
        return results

    def _attach_citation(self, r: SearchResult, query: str) -> None:
        personal = r.match_type.startswith("personal:")
        gov = self.personal_gov if personal else self.gov
        sem = self._personal_semantic if personal else self._semantic
        recorded = None
        if gov is not None and gov.audit is not None:
            recorded = gov.audit.index_get("note", gov.rel(r.path))
        try:
            r.citation = cite(
                r.path,
                chunk_index=r.chunk_index,
                excerpt=r.content_excerpt,
                query=query,
                indexed_sig=sem.file_mtimes.get(r.path) if sem is not None else None,
                recorded=recorded,
            )
        except Exception as e:  # provenance must never break retrieval
            logger.debug("Citation failed for %s: %s", r.path, e)

    def _search_vault(
        self,
        vault: Vault,
        semantic: SemanticIndex | None,
        query: str,
        limit: int,
        hybrid: bool,
        wing: str = None,
        room: str = None,
        keyword: KeywordIndex | None = None,
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Search a single vault.

        Hybrid (semantic + BM25, RRF-fused) when the semantic extra is available,
        BM25 keyword search over note content otherwise, and note-name matching
        as a last resort (e.g. SQLite without FTS5, or no keyword hit).
        """
        self._maybe_refresh(semantic, vault.vault_path, keyword)
        results: list[SearchResult] = []
        if semantic is not None and semantic.available and semantic.chunks:
            results = semantic.search(query, limit, hybrid)
        elif keyword is not None and keyword.available:
            results = keyword.search(query, limit)

        if not results:
            notes = vault.search_by_name(query)
            results = [
                SearchResult(
                    path=str(n.path),
                    content_excerpt=n.content[:200],
                    score=1.0,
                    match_type="name",
                )
                for n in notes[:limit]
            ]

        if wing or room:
            filtered = []
            for r in results:
                if wing and wing not in r.path:
                    continue
                if room and room not in r.path:
                    continue
                filtered.append(r)
            results = filtered or results[:limit]

        return results

    def _maybe_refresh(
        self,
        semantic: SemanticIndex | None,
        vault_path: Path,
        keyword: KeywordIndex | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Re-index new/changed/deleted notes if the last check is old enough.

        One directory walk is shared by the semantic and keyword indexes.
        """
        now = time.monotonic()
        key = (id(semantic), id(keyword))
        last = self._last_refresh.get(key)
        if last is not None and now - last < self.index_refresh_interval:
            return
        self._last_refresh[key] = now
        try:
            snapshot = scan_vault(vault_path)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Vault scan for index refresh failed: %s", e)
            return
        for index in (keyword, semantic):
            if index is None:
                continue
            try:
                changes = index.refresh(vault_path, snapshot=snapshot)
                if any(changes.values()):
                    logger.debug("%s refreshed: %s", type(index).__name__, changes)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.debug("Index refresh skipped: %s", e)

    def qsearch(self, query: str, limit: int = 5) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """QMD-style semantic search. Convenience method."""
        return self.search(query, limit, hybrid=True)

    def rebuild_index(self) -> int:
        """Rebuild the search indexes (keyword, and semantic when enabled).

        Returns the number of notes indexed.
        """
        self.gov.require("write", "rebuild_index")
        keyword_count = self.keyword.index_vault(self.vault_path)
        semantic = self.semantic  # access property once; narrows Optional
        if semantic is None:
            return keyword_count
        semantic.clear()
        count = semantic.index_vault(self.vault_path)
        semantic.save_index()
        return count or keyword_count
